steps.title: Prepare stock and working solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the following stock solutions in advance: 1× PBS; 1× PBS with 0.3 % Triton X‑100 (PBST); DAPI stock (1 mg/mL); dNTP stock; rhodamine‑conjugated anti‑DIG antibody (100 µg/mL); blocking solution; DABCO solution. Prepare fresh solutions on the day of use: 4 % paraformaldehyde fixative; 1× PBS with magnesium chloride. Prepare immediately before use: primary antibody solution; secondary antibody solution (anti‑rabbit AF647); nick‑translation reaction mixture; rhodamine‑conjugated anti‑DIG antibody working solution.

steps.title: Block tissues before primary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate dissected Drosophila larval tissues in blocking buffer for 2 h at room temperature (RT). This reduces background and improves signal‑to‑background ratio.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Remove blocking buffer and add 50 µL of anti‑γH2Av primary antibody diluted in blocking solution; incubate for 12 h at 4 °C (alternatively, 1 h at 37 °C).

steps.title: Wash and block before secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Perform three washes with 0.3 % PBST, each for 10–15 min at RT. Then incubate tissues in blocking solution for 1 h at RT.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: In the dark, add 50 µL of anti‑rabbit AF647 secondary antibody diluted in blocking solution; incubate for 2 h at RT. Choose a secondary that does not overlap with the nick‑labeling signal.

steps.title: Wash post‑secondary incubation
steps.instruction: In the dark, wash tissues three times with 0.3 % PBST, each wash lasting 10–15 min at RT.

steps.title: Wash with MgCl₂‑PBS before nick translation
steps.instruction: Wash tissues twice with 1× PBS supplemented with 0.5 mM magnesium chloride, each wash for 5 min. Magnesium ions enhance DNA polymerase I activity.

steps.title: Prepare and add nick‑translation mixture
steps.instruction: Prepare the nick‑translation reaction mixture as described in the Materials and Equipment section just before use (keep on ice). Add 25 µL of this mixture to each 200 µL microcentrifuge tube containing the tissues.

steps.title: Incubate nick‑translation reaction
steps.instruction: In the dark, incubate the tubes at 37 °C for 2 h using a thermocycler (or a water bath, noting that a water bath may be less effective).

steps.title: Wash after nick translation and block
steps.instruction: Remove the reaction mixture and wash tissues three times with 0.3 % PBST, each wash for 10 min at RT. Then incubate tissues in blocking solution for 1 h at RT.

steps.title: Incubate with rhodamine anti‑DIG and DAPI
steps.instruction: In the dark, incubate tissues for 2 h at RT with rhodamine‑conjugated anti‑DIG antibody (Fab fragments, 0.5 µg/mL) diluted in blocking solution and containing DAPI (1 µg/mL).

steps.title: Wash after labeling
steps.instruction: Remove antibody solution and wash tissues three times with 0.3 % PBST, each wash for 10 min at RT (performed in the dark).

steps.title: Acquire confocal images
steps.instruction: Mount slides and image on a confocal microscope (Zeiss LSM 900) using the following settings: anti‑DIG‑Rhodamine (λ 545 nm, red channel), anti‑rabbit AF647 (λ 647 nm, far‑red channel); set pinhole to 1; adjust gain to avoid saturation; set detector ranges per channel; use a 40×/1.3 oil objective, zoom 0.5×; acquire Z‑stacks with 2 µm optical section interval; save images in appropriate formats.

steps.title: Process images and quantify rhodamine‑positive nuclei
steps.instruction: Open the acquired .czi files in Fiji/ImageJ; select the region of interest (e.g., front region of the morphogenetic furrow of eye disc); split channels to isolate red (rhodamine) and blue (DAPI); manually count rhodamine‑positive nuclei throughout the Z‑stack using the multipoint tool.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze quantified data with GraphPad Prism 9 or Microsoft Excel 2019; use unpaired two‑tailed Student’s t‑tests; denote significance as * (p ≤ 0.05), ** (p ≤ 0.01), *** (p ≤ 0.001), **** (p ≤ 0.0001), ns (p > 0.05). Prepare figures with Adobe Illustrator cc 2018 and BioRender as needed.

description: In situ nick translation (ISNT) is a highly sensitive technique for detecting DNA strand breaks. In nick translation, the DNA break site is synthesized to a 3′-hydroxyl end in the presence of template using DNA polymerase I. During this process, the labeled nucleotide is incorporated into the synthesizing strand, and detection of this labeled nucleotide confirms the DNA strand breaks. It has been utilized for various applications, including making probes for the hybridization technique and molecular cytogenetics, as well as detecting apoptosis and necrosis mediated cell death.2,3,4,5,6,7 This protocol can easily detect both apoptotic and non-apoptotic DNA strand breaks. Here, we have standardized to label DNA strand breaks in the Drosophila larval hematopoietic organ called the lymph gland, and efficiently detected them during development. Additionally, we observed nick translation in eye imaginal discs during cell death. This low-cost, kit-free protocol can also be applied to other Drosophila tissues. We have detailed the complete protocol here, including solution preparation, dissection of the Drosophila larval tissues, immunostaining, incubation and labeling, imaging, and data analysis.
